Article Title: Centre, UT govt have made J&K safer, says US envoy
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR/NEW DELHI: In a rare public affirmation of India's sovereignty over J&K by a top US diplomat, ambassador Sergio Gor said Wednesday the UT is an important part of India and said Washington will consider downgrading its highest "do not travel" warning for J&K.Gor made the remarks in a joint briefing with J&K CM Omar Abdullah in Srinagar, during what's the first standalone visit by a US envoy to the UT after abrogation of Art 370 in 2019. His remarks are seen by Indian officials as validating India's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and post-2018 counterterror strategy and governance reforms. Later, Pakistan summoned the US Charge d'Affaires in Islamabad and lodged a demarche.Pakistan summoned the US Charge d’Affaires in Islamabad to lodge a “strong protest” over what it described as factually incorrect, referring to remarks by Gor on the status of J&K. Pakistan also claimed Gor’s “irresponsible” statement negated the long-standing position of US on J&K.“US puts out travel warnings and every so often, we re-evaluate those travel warnings. I cannot make any big announcements here today, but it is something we are going to look at,” said Gor who will visit Ladakh Thursday.“New Delhi, the chief minister here, the govt here, we believe have made some incredible steps to keeping this area safer and making it more safe,” added Gor.In remarks that could signal to other western countries to re-evaluate their own travel advisories, Gor said a lot of Americans would “enjoy coming here and seeing the beauty and the opportunities that exist here”.“So, we will be looking at if the travel warning that is imposed and recommended by US is something that should be downgraded because, as I said earlier, this is a beautiful area,” he said.US State Department currently maintains Level-4 travel warning for J&K. To downgrade the advisory, according to American authorities, US verifies sustained reductions in terror incidents, long-term political stability, ease of movement for foreign nationals, and reliable emergency consular access. Gor called on Abdullah at his residence soon after reaching Srinagar.“I am thrilled to be here. We just had a very good meeting and we have some follow-ups that we hope to take back to Washington (and) back to Delhi. But a very warm, a very cordial meeting and we look forward to building this relationship forward,” he said.Abdullah said he discussed with Gor the relations between Delhi and Washington with a specific focus on J&K. “It was a very good meeting. We had an opportunity to discuss the relations between our two countries, but with a specific focus on what US can do with J&K,” the CM said.“There are obviously certain legacy issues that over time we will be working to resolve. But we look forward to taking this conversation further...” Abdullah said.
Article Summary: Us state department currently maintains level-4 travel warning for j&k. Pakistan summoned the us charge d’affaires in islamabad to lodge a “strong protest” over what it described as factually incorrect. Pakistan also claimed gor’s “irresponsible” statement negated the long-standing position of us on j &k.

Article Title: Trump tariffs: India seeks WTO consultations over 50% US duties quota on quartz surface imports
Article Text:
India exported around $380 million worth of quartz surface products to the US in FY26.

What the 50% tariff quota for quartz surface products is about

As the Donald Trump administration continues to find ways to impose tariffs, India has approached the World Trade Organization (WTO) seeking consultations with the US over Washington’s tariff-rate quota on imports of quartz surface products. The measure took effect on August 15 and is set to remain in force for four years.India exported around $380 million worth of quartz surface products to the US in FY26. The US has identified India, Vietnam, Spain and Thailand as major exporters of these products.US President Donald Trump issued a proclamation on July 31 introducing a tariff-rate quota of up to 50% on quartz surface product imports from several countries.Also Read | 100% tariffs: Why India may ignore Trump threat and continue buying Russian crude oil The move came after the US International Trade Commission said that imports of these products had risen sufficiently to become a substantial cause of serious injury to US producers of similar or directly competing products.In its August 14 communication to the WTO, New Delhi said it has a "substantial interest" in the matter and suggested that the consultations be conducted virtually at a time mutually convenient to both sides, according to an ET report."India would like to propose that the consultations mentioned above take place virtually as per mutual convenience of both sides," India told the WTO while requesting consultations under the WTO agreement on safeguards.This is the fourth instance in which India has sought such consultations with Washington. Earlier cases involved steel and aluminium, automobiles and auto components, and copper imports.WTO rules provide an exemption from safeguard measures for developing countries whose individual share of the relevant imports is below 3%, provided that the combined share of all such developing countries does not cross 9% of total imports.Washington has imposed a 10% tariff on Indian goods following a Section 301 investigation into forced labour and is also moving ahead with legislation that could impose tariffs of as much as 100% on India and four other countries identified as major buyers of Russian oil and gas. At the same time, India and the US are engaged in negotiations for a trade agreement.The US last week also included India among more than 40 countries that it identified as part of a "shadow trans-shipment network", alleging that the network enables Chinese goods to enter the US while avoiding tariffs. Washington has said it plans to use artificial intelligence to detect and take action against such shipments.Also Read | Beijing’s billion-barrel weapon: Why India must prepare for China-driven oil prices
Article Summary: Us president donald trump issued a proclamation on july 31 introducing a tariff-rate quota of up to 50% on quartz surface product imports from several countries. The measure took effect on august 15 and is set to remain in force for four years. India exported around $380 million worth of quartz surface products to the us in fy26.

Article Title: 'Every voter had valid photo ID': Trump cites Indian election system to make case for 'Save America Act'
Article Text:
Trump praises India’s election system, pushes SAVE America Act

What is Save America Act

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday praised India’s election system and called for the passage of the SAVE America Act, which seeks to require proof of citizenship and voter identification in US elections.In a post on Truth Social, Trump cited a recent conversation involving Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and highlighted India’s use of photo identification for voters.Trump said, "Earlier this month, India’s Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, asked our Administration, How can you have Elections in the US without a valid Photo ID?"Referring to the last general election, Trump said, "India's last Election had 646,000,000 Voters! Less than 1 per cent voted by mail, and every single Voter had to have a VALID Photo Identity Document."Trump also renewed his call for Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, saying, "We need to pass THE SAVE AMERICA ACT, now!"According to the White House, the proposed legislation seeks to ensure that only US citizens are eligible to vote in federal elections. "American citizens and only American citizens should decide American elections," the White House said, describing the bill as a "common sense, bipartisan bill."The legislation would require voters to provide valid identification and proof of US citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections. It also proposes limiting mail-in voting to certain circumstances, including illness, disability, military service and travel, according to news agency ANI.The White House said the bill would further require states to remove non-citizens from federal voter rolls. "If you want to register to vote in the United States, you have to be a citizen in the United States," it said.The administration also compared US election practices with those of other countries, arguing that the US has weaker voter-identification safeguards. "India and Brazil tie voter ID to a biometric database, while the United States largely relies on self-attestation for citizenship," the White House said.The bill was introduced in Congress on January 29. Trump has repeatedly backed the SAVE America Act, arguing that stricter voter-ID and citizenship requirements are necessary to strengthen election security.The SAVE America Act is a proposed US law aimed at tightening voting rules in federal elections. It would:MAGA supremo Donald Trump has urged both Republicans and Democrats to support the bill, arguing that only US citizens should decide US elections.The bill also compares US election rules with those in other countries. It says India and Brazil link voter IDs to biometric databases, while the US largely relies on self-attestation of citizenship. It also points to stricter ballot and mail-voting rules in countries such as Germany, Canada, Denmark and Sweden.
Article Summary: Trump praises india’s election system, pushes save america act. Bill would require voters to show valid id before registering. Require proof of us citizenship. Restrict mail-in voting, with exceptions for illness, disability, military service or travel.

Article Title: 'Not a single protester died': Rijiju defends Delhi police response to Jantar Mantar protests
Article Text:
Rijiju defends police response to student protests (ANI image)

NEW DELHI: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Tuesday defended the Bihar and Delhi governments and law enforcement agencies over their handling of student protests, saying security forces managed large crowds without any casualties or serious injuries."Not a single person died; not a single person suffered a broken bone. Not even one protester is in the hospital with a serious injury. Consider the scale of this movement: thousands turned up, and so many criminals infiltrated under the guise of students," he said as cited by news agency ANI.Rijiju praised the police and administration for their handling of the protests, while contrasting it with the response to demonstrations under previous Congress-led governments."If such a movement had taken place during the Congress era, and many did, resulting in thousands of deaths, one should praise the Delhi police and the administration for handling such a massive protest without allowing even a single serious injury. Thousands actually died from gunfire during the Congress era," Rijiju said."It is the Congress that imposes an Emergency in response to protests. You might recall how many people have fallen victim to gunfire during the various movements that have taken place in this country.Even during the movement to create the state of Telangana, so many people were killed... In this movement, not a single shot was fired," he added.Rijiju said that despite the presence of thousands of protesters, including what he described as political agitators from the Aam Aadmi Party, Bhim Army and Samajwadi Party, as well as “dafli-playing agitators”, the Delhi Police used minimal force. He said force was used only when demonstrators attempted to break through barricades and march towards Parliament."Furthermore, more than half the people, whether from the Aam Aadmi Party, the dafli-playing agitators, the Bhim Army, or the Samajwadi Party, came and incited others to violence; yet, not a single casualty occurred," Rijiju added.On the Gen-Z movement and its demand for education reforms, Rijiju said the Narendra Modi-led NDA government remained committed to the welfare of the country’s youth.He also called for strict judicial action against those responsible for examination leaks and reiterated the government’s zero-tolerance stance on violence during public protests."We respect the students' sentiments. The Prime Minister introduced such a good law and took step after step, promising to work for their future," Rijiju said.The remarks came amid student protests in Bihar over alleged examination irregularities and the NEET paper leak controversy.Clashes were reported between protesters and police in Siwan on July 25 following stone-pelting, after which police used tear gas and lathi charges to disperse the crowd. An AK-47 firing incident was also reported during the unrest.The remarks come weeks after the CJP called off its 37-day protest at Jantar Mantar on July 25, following the resignation of then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and assurances on some of the protesters’ other demands.The agitation was centred on the NEET paper leak issue and drew students and young volunteers from across the country, along with support from opposition leaders. Activist Sonam Wangchuk joined the protest on June 28 and began an indefinite hunger strike. He was later shifted to Safdarjung Hospital after his health deteriorated.The protest also saw police action on July 20 when demonstrators attempted to march towards Parliament. The Congress and other opposition parties later raised the issue in Parliament, contributing to disruptions during proceedings.
Article Summary: Union parliamentary affairs minister kiren rijiju defends police response to student protests. He says security forces managed large crowds without any casualties or serious injuries. Comments come amid student protests in bihar over alleged examination irregularities and the neet paper leak controversy.

Article Title: 'Will review travel advisory': US envoy Gor visits Srinagar, says J&K 'important part of India'

US Ambassador Sergio Gor visits Srinagar with J&K CM Omar

NEW DELHI: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor met Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah in Srinagar on Wednesday, his first visit to the region since taking office. Gor said that Washington would reconsider its travel advisories for the Union Territory."It's a pleasure to be here. This is an important part of India. I am here, visiting for the first time. It is an incredibly beautiful place. I am thrilled to be here," Gor told reporters after the meeting."We just had a very good meeting. We have some follow-ups, so we hope to take back to Washington, back to Delhi. But a very warm, a very cordial and we look forward to building this relationship forward," he said.Gor said the US would reconsider its advisories on travel to Jammu and Kashmir, which have historically cautioned American citizens against visiting the region."The United States puts out travel warnings and every so often, we re-evaluate those travel warnings. I cannot make any big announcements here today, but it is something we are going to look at."New Delhi, the chief minister here, the government here, we believe have made some incredible steps to keeping this area safer and making it more safe," Gor said at a joint media briefing with Abdullah."So, we will be looking at if the travel warning that is imposed and recommended by the United States is something that should be downgraded because, as I said earlier, this is a beautiful area.I think a lot of Americans would enjoy coming here and seeing the beauty and the opportunities that exist here," the US envoy added.In a post on X, he said he appreciated the opportunity to meet Abdullah and learn more about his priorities."We discussed ways to deepen economic collaboration and create opportunities that would mutually benefit both of our nations," Gor wrote.CM Abdullah described the meeting as “very good”, saying the discussions focused on what the US could do for Jammu and Kashmir.“As Ambassador Gor has said, it was a very good meeting. We had an opportunity to discuss the issues that we have, with a specific focus on what the US can do with Jammu and Kashmir,” Abdullah said.He added that there were “certain legacy issues” that they will be working on to resolve, while expressing hope that engagement between the US and J&K would move further."This is a conversation that will take place both between Ambassador Gor and Washington, and between me and the Govt of India in New Delhi. But we are very hopeful and optimistic that the engagement between the US and J&K will both widen and deepen in the years ahead.", Abdullah added.The visit is seen as a significant diplomatic engagement, with the US envoy meeting the chief minister of a region that has been at the centre of India-Pakistan tensions. It also signals a potential shift in Washington's approach to travel advisories for the Union Territory.
Article Summary: Us ambassador to india sergio gor met jammu and kashmir chief minister omar abdullah in srinagar on wednesday. Gor said that washington would reconsider its travel advisories for the union territory. The visit is seen as a significant diplomatic engagement, with the us envoy meeting the chief minister of a region that has been at the centre of india-pakistan tensions.

Article Title: 'There's a problem at the border': Rijiju admits delineation issue in Arunachal, rejects China incursion claim
Article Text:
Rijiju explained that the lack of demarcation has led to Chinese claims over certain stretches of land

NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Wednesday rejected reports that China has made a 60-km incursion into Arunachal Pradesh, saying there is a problem at the border but only because the boundary has not been delineated. He said concerns raised by villagers living in the frontier state are valid, but warned against spreading misinformation about Chinese troops entering Indian territory."Those who say that China has entered 60 kilometres inside (India) and share various videos to defame us are wrong. There is a problem at the border. Some people from villages in Arunachal Pradesh have expressed concern about the border problem, and that concern is valid because the border has not been delineated," he told news agency IANS.Rijiju said the situation should not be interpreted as China having captured an Indian village. He explained that the lack of demarcation has led to Chinese claims over certain stretches of land."So, it is not like they (China) came and captured our village. That is not the case. On certain land, they have cast an eye because there is no demarcation. Our people believe that our land extends further ahead, while the villages situated on the China side, including Tibetan and local people, claim that their land extends deep inside here.So, there is confusion," the Union minister said."But telling such lies that they have entered 60 kilometres inside, and posting unrelated photos from Bangladesh and elsewhere to claim that the Chinese Army has penetrated 60 kilometres inside Arunachal, spreading such misinformation lowers the morale of our Army personnel and security forces stationed there, and creates confusion in the country. This is not right," he added.He said India has strengthened security arrangements along the frontier, with the Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) increasing patrolling in the area.His comments come amid renewed focus on the India-China border following the government's decision to formally identify 27 locations and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard names on official Survey of India maps.The move followed China's repeated attempts to assign its own names to places in Arunachal Pradesh.India has repeatedly stressed that Arunachal Pradesh is an inalienable part of India.The ministry of external affairs has also stressed that maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control is essential for the broader India-China relationship. India has said the state of affairs along the border will have a bearing on the wider bilateral ties.“Let me reiterate this once again that Arunachal Pradesh is an inalienable and integral part of India and this is a fact that is self-evident. At the same time, let me also underline that nothing can change this indisputable reality,” the MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in a media briefing on August 11.
Article Summary: Rijiju explained that the lack of demarcation has led to chinese claims over certain stretches of land. He warned against spreading misinformation about chinese troops entering indian territory. His comments come amid renewed focus on the india-china border following the government's decision to formally identify 27 locations and geographical features.

Article Title: 'We need to meet': Envoy says PM Modi wants Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman's visit to be 'memorable'
Article Text:
File photo: PM Modi and Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman

India calls for trust, dialogue amid strains

Trade and youth seen as bridge between neighbours

Dhaka seeks ‘propitious environment’ for Rahman visit

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi wants Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s proposed visit to India to be “memorable”, Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi said, as uncertainty continues over the trip amid fresh strains in ties between New Delhi and Dhaka.Speaking at a reception hosted by the Indian High Commission in Dhaka on Tuesday for Bangladeshi business leaders and a visiting Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) delegation, Trivedi said PM Modi had emphasised the need for the two leaders to meet and assured Rahman of an appropriate welcome.“Prime Minister Modi just mentioned one thing. We need to meet. And you can tell them on my behalf that you have the prime minister of India's assurance that when the honourable prime minister of Bangladesh visits India, he will have such an honourable reception as he deserves,” Trivedi said, as quoted by news agency PTI.He added that PM Modi wanted Rahman's visit to be “memorable”, stressing that closer engagement between the two leaders would ultimately benefit people and businesses in both countries.“Ultimately, the benefit will go to people and businesses. Business people all over the world have a big role to play in bridging this gap,” Trivedi said.Trivedi's remarks come amid uncertainty over Rahman's proposed visit to New Delhi for the Brics summit on September 12-13 and a possible bilateral meeting with PM Modi.The proposed visit has become complicated by Dhaka's demand for the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who has been living in India since she was ousted in August 2024 following violent student-led protests.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition after she was sentenced to death in absentia by a special tribunal in November 2025 over alleged “crimes against humanity” during the crackdown on protesters.India has said the extradition request is being examined in accordance with applicable law and established legal procedures.Dhaka has also recently objected to a virtual media interaction by Hasina from New Delhi on August 5, saying it hurt the sentiments of Bangladeshis and could affect efforts to improve bilateral ties. Ministry of external affairs has said it had no role in the event and does not endorse comments made there about the Bangladesh government.Against this backdrop, Trivedi called for both countries to address their differences while continuing to engage with each other.“I am not telling that you forget the past, but keep the past and sort out the differences of the past. But move on. Don't get stagnant,” he said.He described disagreements as natural between “vibrant democracies” and said they could be addressed through dialogue and engagement.“We deeply understand the concerns of brothers and sisters of Bangladesh. Definitely, there are concerns. But this is a partnership of equals,” Trivedi said.He also stressed the importance of trust, saying, “The foundation of any long-lasting relation is mutual and unconditional trust.”Trivedi highlighted India's Neighbourhood First policy and said the two countries should build on their shared history, culture and aspirations despite recent “hiccups”.“We have shared history, we have shared culture, and this is where we need to foster,” he said.He also pointed to Bangladesh's younger population, saying India wanted to work with the “new Bangladesh” to create greater opportunities for its youth.“This is a new Bangladesh. And this new Bangladesh has the youth. And youth has also gone through a lot of struggles and a lot of sacrifice. So, our objective obviously [is] to have peace and prosperity and the youth must get that opportunity,” he said.The envoy urged businesses in both countries to play a greater role in rebuilding confidence and expanding economic ties. A CII delegation is currently in Dhaka to explore opportunities for increased trade, investment and industrial cooperation.“We don't only share border, we share dreams, we share aspirations and equality,” Trivedi said, underlining the importance of people-to-people ties.The remarks come days after Bangladesh attached conditions to Rahman's possible visit to India, amid pressure from domestic political groups over the unresolved Hasina extradition issue.Bangladesh's foreign affairs spokesperson AKM Shahidul Karim had said officials from the two countries had been in contact over the possibility of a bilateral visit but insisted that a “propitious environment” needed to be created.Dhaka said the August 5 media interaction by Hasina had affected that environment and called on India to act expeditiously on its extradition request.Indian government sources, however, have maintained that the invitation to Rahman for the Brics summit and a bilateral visit remains in place, with the timing ultimately for Dhaka to decide.The competing positions highlight the diplomatic challenge facing the two neighbours: India is signalling that it wants to keep the relationship moving forward through political and economic engagement, while Dhaka continues to press New Delhi on issues surrounding Hasina.For now, Trivedi's message is that despite the differences, India wants Rahman's proposed visit to go ahead on terms that allow the two sides to rebuild trust and focus on wider bilateral interests.
Article Summary: India calls for trust, dialogue amid strains in ties with bangladesh. Indian high commissioner dinesh trivedi says pm modi wants visit to be'memorable' trip has become complicated by dhaka's demand for extradition of former pm hasina. A cii delegation is currently in dhaka to explore opportunities for increased trade, investment and industrial cooperation.

Article Title: India will take whatever action to defeat terrorism: MEA as trial move begins against Hafiz Saeed, Lakhvi
Article Text:
Mumbai Police has written to Special Public Prosecutor to initiate the process against the accused who remain absconding including Hafiz Saeed and Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi.(File photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India will continue to take “whatever action is required” to defeat terrorism, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday as Mumbai Police initiated proceedings for an in absentia trial against six Pakistan-based accused in the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks case.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal made the remarks during the ministry's biweekly media briefing while responding to questions on the move against the absconding accused, including Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) founder Hafiz Saeed and senior operative Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi.“These are very serious things. We take it very seriously. We want the global community to understand the gravity of such actions. India has been hit hard by terrorism. We have, over the last several years, taken a lot of effort to galvanise, to strengthen global action to fight terrorism, including cross-terrorism, and our fight to deal with terrorism will continue further. And whatever action is required to be taken on that account to defeat terrorism, we will continue to take,” Jaiswal said.The MEA's comments came a day after Mumbai Police began the process to initiate an in absentia trial against six Pakistani nationals accused in connection with the November 2008 terror attacks.According to the proceedings, Mumbai Police has written to Special Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam to initiate the process against the accused who remain absconding.The proclamation has been issued against Hafiz Saeed, Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi, Sajid Mir, Abu Alqama, Asim alias Abu Qahafa and Major Abdur Rehman Pasha.The move marks the first time provisions allowing trials in absentia under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, are being invoked in a terror case of this nature, according to the information provided.Nikam said Section 356 of the BNSS provides for proceedings against absconding offenders in their absence, with the objective of preventing prolonged delays in delivering justice.The 26/11 attacks in Mumbai in November 2008 were carried out by Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists, killing more than 160 people and injuring hundreds.India has repeatedly sought action against those accused of planning and facilitating the attacks who remain in Pakistan.The latest proceedings come as New Delhi continues to press for international cooperation in tackling cross-border terrorism and holding those accused of terror attacks accountable.Jaiswal said India wants the international community to recognise the seriousness of terrorist activities and reiterated that New Delhi would continue efforts to strengthen global action against terrorism.During the briefing, Jaiswal also responded to Pakistan's denial of India's allegations linking the Shahzad Bhatti terror network to Pakistan's Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI).He reiterated that the Indian government's position on the matter remained unchanged.“The government of India has put forth this position, and that is where it stands,” Jaiswal said.The comments followed coordinated operations by Indian security agencies across 14 states on Monday, ahead of Independence Day, against what authorities described as an ISI-backed, Pakistan-based Shahzad Bhatti terror network.According to security agencies, 253 people were detained, more than 80 FIRs were registered and over 200 operatives were arrested during the operations.The action was carried out under India's stated policy of “zero tolerance” towards cross-border terrorism.The developments come against the backdrop of India's continuing efforts to pursue those accused of terrorism, including individuals linked to the 26/11 attacks who remain outside the country's jurisdiction.
Article Summary: Mumbai police has written to special public prosecutor to initiate the process against the accused who remain absconding. The proclamation has been issued against hafiz saeed, zaki-ur-rehman lakhvi, sajid mir, abu alqama, asim alias abu qahafa and major abdur rehman pasha.

NEW DELHI: Misleading claims, incorrect product descriptions, ingredient declarations and packaging material have come under the scanner of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ), with several businesses taking corrective action after notices.Lotte India Corporation Pvt Ltd was flagged over “100%” claims and subsequently rectified its labels. Dabur India Ltd was pulled up for selling an Ayurvedic proprietary medicinal oil as edible oil. It informed e-commerce platforms about the product’s correct categorisation and discontinued use of “edible oil”.Ferns N Petals Pvt Ltd was flagged for using hydrogenated vegetable fat instead of cocoa butter and deficiencies in ingredient and nutritional declarations, including recommended dietary allowance and mango percentage. It subsequently revised labels of affected products, including Roasted Almond Chocolate.Eat Better Ventures Pvt Ltd was flagged over a “No Added Sugar” claim and a comparative claim involving ordinary ladoos. It removed the comparative claims and revised its advertising.FSSAI also flagged S S Product Prop over non-food-grade packaging material and mandatory labelling deficiencies, citing a potential contamination concern.The firm said it had been closed since February 2026 and would comply with applicable provisions if the business resumed.Another notice concerned OM Sai Healthcare’s Vedefal capsules, with FSSAI flagging non-compliance with provisions governing health supplements and nutraceuticals and concerns over product claims and declarations. The company acknowledged the observations, revised marketing material and instructed dealers to discontinue previous promotional material.The cases highlight FSSAI’s scrutiny of product claims, categorisation, ingredients, labelling and packaging, with businesses required to address deficiencies following regulatory intervention.
Article Summary: Fssai, having scrutinised product claims, categorisation, ingredients, labelling and packaging, has required businesses to address deficiencies following regulatory intervention. Lotte india corporation pvt ltd was flagged over “100%” claims and subsequently rectified its labels.

Article Title: Is Ice Poseidon ‘wanted’ in Japan? Viral poster puts spotlight on streamer’s past police confrontations
Article Text:
Is Ice Poseidon ‘wanted’ in Japan? Viral poster puts spotlight on streamer’s past police confrontations

Paul Michael Joseph Denino faces no official wanted status in Japan

Ice Poseidon’s recent Japan trip and Pokémon store incident

Ice Poseidon is not officially wanted or under arrest in Japan, despite a “wanted poster” circulating online. The image was shared by DramaAlert on August 19, 2026, but there is no evidence that it is a Japanese police notice or that Paul Michael Joseph Denino has an active arrest warrant in the country. Japan’s National Police Agency publishes official wanted information, and Ice Poseidon does not appear on its listed wanted suspects. His recent livestreams also show him continuing to travel around Japan. The confusion comes from his past clashes with police, businesses and locals, along with unofficial citizen-made lists targeting nuisance streamers.The “wanted poster” should not be confused with an official Japanese police document. Japanese accounts that track foreign nuisance streamers have also discussed the image and questioned its wording. The account @canceljohnnys has separately posted about Ice Poseidon and his activities in Japan. These citizen-run accounts are not part of Japanese law enforcement.Ice Poseidon has faced several problems in Japan before. During his 2025 Japan and Korea livestream tour, police questioned him and another streamer after they picked and ate mandarins from trees without clear permission.Dexerto reported that about 14 officers became involved after a complaint, with translation devices used during the questioning. There was no reported arrest or criminal charge from that incident.He and other streamers were also stopped from boarding a ferry at Kagoshima during the same trip. JAPAN Forward reported that the group was refused boarding after previous incidents involving disruptive behaviour. (MThose incidents help explain why Ice Poseidon has appeared on citizen-created “wanted” or nuisance lists. One such list in February 2025 was titled “Harassing Japanese Locals” and included Ice Poseidon, Johnny Somali and other streamers. Dexerto reported that the list was created by a Japanese citizen, not the police.Ice Poseidon has returned to Japan in August 2026 and has continued streaming publicly. One recent incident involved a Pokémon store, where security stopped him after apparently recognising him from a photograph. He later returned wearing different clothes, a hat and sunglasses and managed to enter the store. The incident did not involve a reported police arrest or criminal charge.That distinction matters. A private store can refuse entry, while a citizen group can publish its own warning list. Neither action means someone is officially wanted by Japanese police.Ice Poseidon has faced more serious legal trouble in other countries. He was arrested in Thailand in 2023 over an explicit livestream incident, but that case was later dropped. That history is separate from his current situation in Japan.As of August 20, 2026, there is no verified evidence that Ice Poseidon has been arrested, formally charged or placed on an official Japanese wanted list. The poster circulating online should therefore not be presented as proof of an arrest warrant.
Article Summary: Ice poseidon is not officially wanted or under arrest in japan, despite a “wanted poster” circulating online. The confusion comes from his past clashes with police, businesses and locals, along with unofficial citizen-made lists targeting nuisance streamers. The poster should not be confused with an official japanese police document.

Article Title: How could Patrick Mahomes’ $43.56M restructure help the Chiefs make another bold move? Here’s what could come next

How could Patrick Mahomes’ $43.56M restructure help the Chiefs make another bold move? Here’s what could come next (Via X)

The Kansas City Chiefs have less than $4 million in effective salary-cap space, but that number may not stay there for long. Patrick Mahomes already helped the team create $43.56 million in room with his latest restructure. Now, assistant general manager Chris Shea has confirmed that Kansas City has more ways to create flexibility before the 2026 regular season. That could give Brett Veach another chance to improve the roster.The Chiefs entered the 2026 offseason nearly $60 million over the salary cap. They have since cleared significant money through contract changes and roster decisions. Still, Kansas City has not closed the door on another move. With the final roster taking shape, the front office has several ways to make more room if it sees a player worth adding.Mahomes gave Kansas City its biggest cap boost on Feb. 18. The Chiefs converted $44.05 million of his base salary and a $10.4 million roster bonus into a signing bonus. The move created $43.56 million in 2026 cap space and reduced Mahomes’ 2026 cap hit to $34.65 million.It marked the fifth restructure of Mahomes’ NFL career. The move also showed how strongly Kansas City wants to keep adding pieces around its franchise quarterback.The Chiefs did more than restructure Mahomes’ deal. They released Jawaan Taylor and Mike Danna, clearing about $29 million, while Drue Tranquill agreed to a pay cut worth more than $2 million. Trey Smith had also restructured his contract the previous year, creating another $735,000 in cap room.That history gives Veach and Shea plenty of options. The Chiefs can restructure another veteran contract, make a roster cut or use a combination of moves to create room.There is also a clear reason to keep some flexibility. Chris Jones carries a $44.85 million cap hit in 2026, while Mahomes sits at $34.65 million. Trey Smith, Nick Bolton, Jaylon Moore and Creed Humphrey also carry significant cap numbers.Kansas City does not need to make another huge move simply for the sake of spending. However, one more restructure could give the team breathing room for the regular season or allow Veach to react if a useful player becomes available.Shea addressed the Chiefs’ cap situation on Aug. 19 after training camp practice. With Kansas City sitting at just under $4 million in effective cap space, he made it clear that the front office already has a plan.“We feel good about where we’re at,” Shea said during his Aug. 19 press conference. “Obviously, the rules change a little bit when the season starts. Certain things come onto the cap that aren’t there now. You know, we have a plan to create ample space for us to be able to operate with those charges that come on and create some flexibility.“You know, we have lots of avenues to create more flexibility and more cap space. We may take advantage of some or all in the next few weeks, but we certainly have the ability and likely will create some cap space to get us into the regular season.”That final line gives the Chiefs’ plan away. Kansas City will likely create more room before the regular season starts.The team also has another advantage during roster cuts. After finishing 6-11 in 2025, the Chiefs hold the eighth waiver priority, their best position in years. Assistant GM Mike Bradway said on Aug. 19 that the team remains open to waiver claims and trades during the roster-cut process.So, another Chiefs move does not necessarily mean a blockbuster signing. It could mean clearing enough money to claim a player, complete a trade or handle regular-season charges without financial pressure.Mahomes already did his part in February. Now Veach and Shea have the tools to make another move if the right opportunity appears.
Article Summary: Patrick mahomes' $43.56m restructure gives the chiefs another route to create cap space. Assistant general manager chris shea confirms the chiefs could make another move before week 1. The chiefs entered the 2026 offseason nearly $60 million over the salary cap.

Article Title: Trouble brewing for Zelenskyy? Ex-defence minister calls for wartime polls
Article Text:
Ukraine has been under martial law since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022

Why Fedorov’s election call matters

Why a wartime election would be extremely difficult

Zelenskyy faces a wider political test

Ukraine’s recently dismissed former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov has called for presidential elections to be held despite the ongoing war with Russia, delivering one of the most direct political challenges to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy since the full-scale invasion began in 2022.In a nine-minute video address posted online, Fedorov argued that Ukraine must restore a “full democratic process” even while fighting Russia. “Democracy cannot be held hostage by Russia. We are fighting precisely because we want to remain a free European state,” the 35-year-old said. Although he did not name Zelenskyy, his remarks amounted to a sharp criticism of the way the country is being governed, including concerns over corruption, appointments and a lack of accountability.Fedorov’s intervention comes weeks after Zelenskyy abruptly removed him as defence minister, only six months after his appointment. His dismissal triggered rare wartime protests in Kyiv and has fuelled speculation about growing tensions within Ukraine’s political establishment. Zelenskyy has not publicly responded to the call for elections.Ukraine has been under martial law since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, and elections are suspended under the country’s legal framework.Zelenskyy’s five-year presidential term formally expired in May 2024, but the continuation of martial law has prevented a vote from taking place.Fedorov argued that the prolonged war should not permanently put democratic politics on hold. “We must find a legal, safe and realistic mechanism that will allow Ukraine to restore a full democratic process even amid a prolonged war,” he said.The appeal could prove politically significant because Fedorov is not an outsider. A former digital minister and one of the prominent young reformers in Zelenskyy’s team, he played a key role in Ukraine’s wartime adoption of drone technology and other innovations. His sudden removal, reportedly amid tensions with military leadership, had already exposed divisions within the government.Recent polling cited in the material suggests Fedorov could emerge as a serious contender in a future presidential race. He was placed behind Zelenskyy and former armed forces chief Valerii Zaluzhnyi in a first-round scenario, but polling indicated that both Fedorov and Zaluzhnyi could defeat Zelenskyy in a run-off.Holding an election while the war continues would present enormous logistical and security challenges. Russian missile and drone attacks regularly target Ukrainian cities, while fighting stretches across a front line of more than 1,200km.Millions of Ukrainians have also been displaced. More than 4 million are living under temporary protection in the European Union, while millions more are internally displaced. Around 1 million people are serving in Ukraine’s defence forces, including personnel deployed near the frontline.The situation is further complicated by Russian occupation of roughly a fifth of Ukraine. Ensuring voting rights for people in occupied areas, protecting polling stations and preventing Russian interference would all require new legal and security arrangements.A Ukrainian political analyst cited in the material said there was a deep-rooted view that elections were necessary, but only after the “hot phase” of the war ended. Even Fedorov’s supporters face the question of how a genuinely free and safe vote could be organised while Russian attacks continue.Fedorov’s intervention comes as Zelenskyy faces renewed scrutiny over corruption and the functioning of his administration. Ukraine’s anti-corruption agencies have launched a probe involving current and former officials, including an unnamed official in the presidential office. Zelenskyy subsequently dismissed deputy presidential office head Iryna Mudra, although investigators have not named her as a suspect.The developments add to political pressure on a president whose popularity, while still significant, has fallen from its extraordinary wartime levels. The latest controversy also follows previous public anger over government attempts to curb the powers of anti-corruption agencies.
Article Summary: Ukraine has been under martial law since russia launched its full-scale invasion in february 2022. President volodymyr zelenskyy’s five-year presidential term formally expired in may 2024, but the continuation of martial law has prevented a vote from taking place.

Article Title: "I'm grateful for every lesson": Gisele Bündchen’s candid Tom Brady divorce admission revealed the pain behind her new beginning

Gisele Bündchen opens up about Tom Brady divorce

Gisele Bündchen focuses on her children after divorce

Gisele Bündchen’s divorce from Tom Brady is no longer breaking news, but a deeply emotional 2024 interview still offers a revealing look at what the supermodel went through after their marriage ended. During a conversation with ABC News’ Robin Roberts, Bündchen struggled to hold back tears while reflecting on the end of a 13-year marriage, her children and the new chapter she was trying to build.The interview, released in March 2024 as part of “IMPACT x Nightline: Gisele Bündchen: Climbing the Mountain,” came more than a year after Bündchen and Brady finalized their divorce in October 2022.Their split ended a relationship that had lasted 16 years and a marriage that had lasted 13. By the time Bündchen sat down with Roberts, however, she was trying to understand the experience as part of a larger personal transition rather than simply an ending.Roberts reminded her that she had previously described the divorce as “the death of a dream.” The comment immediately struck an emotional chord.“Well, when you say ...” the model began, before pausing and getting teary. “Sorry, guys, I didn't know ... can I have a little moment?”After collecting herself, Bündchen spoke about accepting a future she had never expected to have.“It's definitely a time of, you know, a transition that had to take place, and it's not something that you — I don't think you wish for that, you know?” she said. “But I think sometimes in life things happen. I feel so blessed because, like, I wouldn't change anything in my life. I had incredible experiences. I learned so much. I have my children, which are the biggest blessings in my life.“And now I get to create — it's a new season, a new chapter in my life, and I get to learn new things, and I get to walk my path in a different way, you know?“And I'm grateful for all of it. I'm grateful for every lesson.”Her words showed that the divorce was not something she viewed in simple terms. There was pain, but there was also gratitude for the years she shared with Brady and the family they created.Bündchen and Brady share two children, Benjamin and Vivian. Brady also has a son, Jack, with actress Bridget Moynahan. For Bündchen, co-parenting meant accepting that the children would grow up moving between two different households and sets of rules.“There's easier days than others. But it's amazing that the kids — they're super smart children,” Bündchen said, laughing. “They know what they can get away with. So I think it's natural that it has different rules, and kids just adapt and they're going to try to do what they want. And I can only control what I do.”She also emphasized the value of her children having relationships with both parents.“It's amazing that they get to spend time with both parents because it's more enriching for their lives, two different worlds, and they get to learn from two different worlds.”Bündchen spoke warmly about Brady’s oldest son, Jack, whom she helped raise during her years with the former NFL star.“I raised him. I love him,” she said.Looking ahead, Bündchen said she wanted to live according to her own values rather than public expectations.“I'm very committed to living my truth more than ever, so I would say that's where my heart is now, where I am right now. I'm living my truth and I'm not apologizing for it,” she explained.The 2024 interview remains significant because it captured Bündchen at a vulnerable point in her life. She was not simply discussing a famous divorce. She was describing the difficult process of accepting change, protecting her children and finding an identity beyond a marriage that had once shaped so much of her public life.
Article Summary: Gisele bündchen and tom brady finalized their divorce in october 2022. The supermodel struggled to hold back tears while reflecting on the end of a 13-year marriage. She said she wanted to live according to her own values rather than public expectations.

Article Title: Volhynia massacres: Russia using WWII to plant discord between Ukraine and Poland?
Article Text:
Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the Volhynia massacres.

How Russia is 'exploiting' the Volhynia dispute

The facts may be real, but the narrative can still be manipulated

Ukraine fatigue creates fertile ground for the campaign

Russia is being accused of using a painful chapter in the history of Poland and Ukraine to deepen tensions between the two countries, as Warsaw and Kyiv remain divided over the killings that took place during World War 2.Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging in Poland around the Volhynia massacres, while also using the issue to fuel anger against Ukrainians living in the country.The campaign has largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in Polish. Analysts say the aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.The historical dispute centres on the Volhynia massacres between 1943 and 1945. Poland says Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Poles during the violence, while thousands of Ukrainians were also killed in retaliatory attacks.Tensions over the issue increased after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy named an army unit after insurgents linked to the massacres. Polish president Karol Nawrocki, who is from the political right, responded by stripping Zelenskyy of a major Polish honour in June.Polish deputy digital minister Pawel Olszewski said the disagreement was quickly followed by a surge in Russian messaging across social media and Russian media platforms, including Telegram.Research by the state-backed Polish Institute of International Affairs found that Polish-language anti-Ukrainian content on X, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube rose by more than 250% after Zelenskyy's decision.Filip Bryjka of PISM said much of this increase appeared to have been artificially boosted through bots, creating the impression that anti-Ukrainian sentiment was spreading rapidly.Analysts say one reason this type of campaign is difficult to detect is that it does not necessarily depend on completely fabricated information.Instead, genuine events and historical grievances can be repeatedly highlighted and framed in ways that encourage anger towards a particular group."The event is real, but the interpretation is imposed by an external actor," said Wojciech Pokora, an analyst at Info Ops Poland Foundation.Moscow has rejected the accusations. The Russian embassy in Warsaw said Russia does not interfere in relations between other countries."The Russian Federation does not interfere in the relations between other states," the Russian embassy in Warsaw said in an emailed statement, adding that accusations about Russia spreading disinformation to undermine support for Ukraine are baseless.The issue has gained greater importance because Poland remains one of Ukraine's strongest supporters in its war against Russia, but public backing for Ukraine has weakened.An IBRiS poll published last month found that 33.6% of respondents said their attitude towards Ukrainians had worsened following the latest dispute linked to the World War Two killings.Another IBRiS survey found that support for continuing military assistance to Ukraine had fallen to 52%, compared with 78% in 2022.Researchers caution that declining support for Ukraine cannot be blamed entirely on Russian influence.Poland is home to an estimated 1.8 to 1.9 million Ukrainian migrants, while disagreements over grain imports and the unresolved legacy of the Volhynia killings have also contributed to public frustration.Olszewski said the Russian messaging had "fallen on fertile ground".Meanwhile, hostility towards Ukrainians in Poland has reportedly increased, prompting prime minister Donald Tusk to call for an end to xenophobic attacks.The issue could become even more politically significant ahead of Poland's 2027 parliamentary elections. Polling suggests Tusk's pro-European government could struggle to retain power, while support for the far-right has been growing.That makes the Volhynia dispute more than a historical argument. For Poland, it touches on a painful national memory. For Ukraine, it is part of a complicated shared history with its neighbour. And for Russia, Polish analysts argue, the disagreement offers an opportunity to deepen divisions between two countries that have otherwise stood together against Moscow.
Article Summary: Polish officials and researchers say moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the volhynia massacres. Campaign largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in polish. Analysts say aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.

Article Title: Kylie Kelce gets emotional recalling the miscarriage that made her terrified to try again

Kylie Kelce admits the fear of trying again after her miscarriage never really went away

Why she keeps returning to this story

A fan question on Kylie Kelce's podcast turned into one of her most honest moments yet. Asked point-blank if she'd been scared to try for another baby after her 2018 miscarriage, the mom of four didn't hedge, she confirmed the fear was real, and it stuck around a lot longer than most people would expect.Kelce first went public with the loss last October, during Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month, explaining that a doctor's visit before the birth of her eldest daughter, Wyatt, confirmed there was no heartbeat.The timing made it worse, the diagnosis fell on her husband Jason's birthday, and she initially couldn't bring herself to break the news to him that day. This week's episode picked up the thread from a different angle: what actually happened once she and Jason decided to try again.According to Kelce, getting pregnant with Wyatt didn't erase the anxiety, it just reshaped it. She views grief from pregnancy loss as something with no real end date, capable of resurfacing unexpectedly no matter how much time has passed or how many kids follow.It's a theme she's returned to more than once, and each time she's shared it, she's said the response from others tends to be more stories of loss rather than awkward silence.She was careful not to frame the fear as the end of the story, either. Her bottom line was that avoiding the risk entirely would have meant never having Wyatt at all, so for her, moving forward despite the fear was worth it. Article Title: Quote of the day by King Charles: "To my darling Mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dear…" - a tribute to Queen Elizabeth, on gratitude, service and a son's farewell
Article Text:
Quote of the day by King Charles (AP photo)

Quote of the day by King Charles

"To my darling Mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dear late Papa, I want simply to say this: Thank you. Thank you for your love and devotion to our family and to the family of nations you have served so diligently all these years. May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest"

What is the meaning of King Charles' quote

Why King Charles thanked Queen Elizabeth II

The personal meaning behind "my darling Mama"

What "the family of nations" actually means

Why Charles' farewell centred on service

The Shakespeare reference at the end of the speech

How the quote reflects the relationship between duty and family

How to apply the message in daily life

Some other memorable quotes by King Charles

"I am a dangerous person because I mind about things."

"It is important to be able to stand back and see the bigger picture."

"The environment is something that is very close to my heart."

"I think we have to be very careful about what we do to the natural world."

Few words spoken at a moment of personal loss carry the weight of an entire lifetime. When Queen Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022, her eldest son, King Charles III, addressed the nation the following day, speaking as both a new monarch and a grieving son at the same time. Recorded in the Blue Drawing Room at Buckingham Palace, with a framed portrait of his mother resting on the desk beside him, his tribute combined personal affection, real gratitude and a recognition of her extraordinary decades of public service. It became one of the most widely remembered moments of that entire period, quoted on front pages across the country the following morning. For millions watching, the address offered a rare glimpse behind the crown, where duty and private grief briefly occupied space. His carefully chosen words also captured the enormous responsibility that had suddenly passed to him, making the moment deeply personal and historically significant.The speech also reassured a grieving public that the values associated with Elizabeth’s reign would continue, while Charles acknowledged the changes that lay ahead. His measured tone reflected both continuity and transition as Britain entered a new chapter.The address also marked the beginning of a new constitutional era, as Charles formally assumed the role his mother had held for seven decades. His message balanced continuity with change, reassuring the public while acknowledging the profound personal loss.At its heart, the message is about gratitude, love and farewell. Charles begins by describing his mother's death as a "last great journey," a gentle way of naming the end of a life, before referring directly to her reunion with her late husband, Prince Philip, who had died in April 2021. Rather than dwelling on the enormous constitutional change actually taking place, Charles places his mother's role firmly within a family context first. He thanks her for the love and devotion she gave to her family, before widening that same gratitude to the people and nations she served. The simplicity of the words "thank you," repeated before he expands on what he is actually grateful for, turns the tribute into an expression of appreciation for an entire lifetime of service.Queen Elizabeth II became monarch in 1952 and remained on the throne for more than seven decades, making her the longest-reigning monarch in British history. Across that period, she served under fifteen British prime ministers and witnessed enormous political, social and technological change. For Charles, though, her significance was never limited to her constitutional role alone. She was also, simply, his mother. His tribute moves between these two identities throughout, recognising her commitment to the "family of nations" she served while speaking about her in the deeply personal language of a son saying goodbye to his parent.The phrase "my darling Mama" gave the speech a genuinely intimate quality that stood apart from the formal language normally associated with royal addresses. Charles was speaking to a global audience, and yet the words themselves were directed towards one single person. Calling his mother "Mama" reflected the private family relationship sitting behind the public institution. Elizabeth II had been Queen to millions of people, but to her son she remained, simply, his mother. That contrast is really what gave the tribute its personal weight rather than letting it feel purely ceremonial.Charles' reference to the "family of nations" reflects Queen Elizabeth II's role across the Commonwealth, a voluntary association of independent countries, many with historical connections to the British Empire, of which she served as Head throughout her entire reign. Her role involved maintaining relationships with leaders and people across every member country, while representing a genuine continuity through decades of political change. Describing these countries as a "family of nations" highlighted exactly the relationships his mother had worked to maintain across the whole of her reign.A central theme running through Queen Elizabeth II's public life was duty. In her 1952 accession broadcast, she pledged her life to the service of the people of the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth. Seven decades later, Charles' farewell returned directly to that same idea. Describing her as having served "so diligently all these years" recognised both the length and the sheer consistency of that commitment. It also reflected the unusual nature of her reign specifically, since she continued carrying out official duties well into her nineties, including appointing Liz Truss as prime minister only two days before her death.Charles closed his tribute with the words "May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The line comes from William Shakespeare's Hamlet, Act 5, Scene 2, spoken by Horatio as he mourns his friend at the play's close, "Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince, and flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The reference gave Charles' speech a genuinely literary and solemn conclusion, connecting his personal farewell to one of the most recognisable expressions of grief in English literature, and its suggestion of a peaceful passage into rest made it particularly fitting for a speech delivered the day after losing a parent.One of the most powerful aspects of Charles' tribute is how it brings together two sides of Queen Elizabeth II's life at once, a mother within her own family, and a monarch with responsibilities reaching far beyond it. Charles' words acknowledge both directly, first thanking her for her "love and devotion to our family," then expanding that same gratitude outward to the people and nations she served. In the same speech, he also announced that Prince William and Catherine would become the new Prince and Princess of Wales, and expressed his love for Harry and Meghan "as they continue to build their lives overseas," a reminder that even a historic constitutional address remained, underneath it, a message about family.The circumstances behind this quote are genuinely unique, but its central message of gratitude applies just as well to ordinary relationships. Say thank you while you still can, since the people who matter most should never have to wait for a farewell to hear how much they are actually appreciated. Recognise quiet, unglamorous forms of service, since care and responsibility are often given without much recognition at all. Value family relationships alongside professional achievement, and remember that simple words of love and appreciation tend to become more meaningful, not less, with time.Why King Charles' farewell remains memorableCharles' first address as King carried an unavoidable constitutional significance, and yet its most memorable passage was deeply personal. He was not simply acknowledging the end of a historic reign. He was saying goodbye to the woman who had been his mother for more than seven decades. The repeated "thank you" captures the central emotion of the entire tribute. After a lifetime defined by public duty, Charles chose to close his first address as monarch with something considerably more private, a reminder that behind every title and institution sits an ordinary human relationship. A queen can be a constitutional figure to an entire nation while remaining, simply, "Mama" to her own son.
Article Summary: Quote of the day by king charles: "to my darling mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dear late papa" queen elizabeth ii died on 8 september 2022, her eldest son, king charles iii, addressed the nation the following day. His tribute combined personal affection, real gratitude and a recognition of her extraordinary decades of public service.

Article Title: F-16 fighter jet crashes in Turkey during training flight, pilot safe
Article Text: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova on Wednesday, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft.In a statement posted on social media, the ministry said the aircraft went down during a routine training mission and that the pilot safely bailed out before the crash.The exact cause of the accident will be determined following a detailed investigation, the ministry added.A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site following the incident, local media reported.Live footage broadcast by Turkish news channel NTV showed a fireball and thick black smoke rising from the wreckage, visible from several locations across the province.
